simple.meaning: אָנַן (ʼânan) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to mourn , i.e. complain.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Numbers, Lamentations, beginning at Numbers 11:1. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אָנַן (H596) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: אָנַן (ʼânan) / H596 is traced through Numbers 11:1, Lamentations 3:39 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: The people were complaining in the ears of Yahweh. When Yahweh heard it, his anger burned; and Yahweh’s fire burned among them, and consumed some of the outskirts of the camp.
